findings.title: README and changelog call malformed math and unprintable values render-only; the language contract says both entry points

serves.scenario: A core user who calls resolveTemplate with ${{(a + b}} or a cyclic value reads in the README that resolveTemplate keeps its old output. The contract says resolveTemplate raises a located type-error for both. One of the two documents contradicts the code, so the card goal of describing behavior exactly fails.

findings.rubric: nothing is described as available that the code does not do; c2 and c3: the documents match the code
findings.reproduction: 1. Read README.md, the paragraph that begins '`render` only.': 'The zero divisor, the malformed expression, the unprintable value and the 15-digit printing apply to `render` ... Core's `resolveTemplate` keeps its old output for these'. 2. Read docs/living/architecture/language-contract.md, Math and output errors: Malformed math ends 'Applies in both entry points.' and Unprintable output ends 'Applies in both entry points.' 3. Read the changelog line 'Math and output errors in `render`: ... a value with no text form ... `resolveTemplate` keeps its old output for these'. 4. Call resolveTemplate('${{(1 + 2}}', new Map()) and resolveTemplate('${{loop}}', a map holding a cyclic object). If either throws, the README and the changelog are wrong; if neither throws, the contract is wrong. Smallest fix: make the README paragraph and the changelog line name only the zero divisor and the 15-digit printing as render-only, if the code matches the contract.
findings.label: f1

replies.restate: README and changelog said malformed math and unprintable values keep old output in resolveTemplate
replies.verify: Ran resolveTemplate: both throw a located type-error; only zero divisor and 15-digit printing differ

findings.title: README says .length on any value other than an array or a text stays null, but an object with its own length key returns that value

serves.scenario: An author passes data {"o": {"length": 5}} and writes ${{o.length}}. The README says this prints empty (null). The contract says it prints 5 (and the same for a JSON object text with its own length key), so the README makes a claim the code contradicts.

findings.rubric: goal-critical question 2: no claim the code contradicts
findings.reproduction: 1. Read the README bullet '**`.length`** is a path segment after any value: an array gives its element count and a text gives ... Any other value, or missing data, stays null'. 2. Read the language contract bullet .length: 'an object with its own key `length` returns that key's value, null included' and 'unless it is a JSON object text with its own key `length`'. 3. Render ${{o.length}} with {"o": {"length": 5}}: the output 5 contradicts the README. Smallest fix: add the own-key exception to the README bullet.
findings.label: f2

replies.restate: README .length bullet omitted the own-key length rule
replies.verify: Ran render: own key 7, JSON text 9, null key empty, text 3, number empty

findings.title: The lexer keyword table in the surfaces test is hand-written, so a keyword the lexer gains without a spec() entry passes

serves.scenario: The card goal is a test that keeps spec() in step with the lexer. BLOCK_PAIRS is a fixed list checked against the lexer, so removing a keyword is caught. If a later card adds a keyword such as MESSAGE to the lexer but not to spec(), every test still passes. The filter half derives its list from FILTER_REGISTRY and has no such gap.

findings.rubric: c1: every lexer keyword appears in spec()
findings.reproduction: Add a new keyword to the lexer's accepted list without adding it to spec.ts or BLOCK_PAIRS, then run tests/language/surfaces.test.ts: it stays green. The test file is frozen, so this is a note for the lead, not a fix request.
evidence: test:ld-spec blocks: spec().blocks has no name outside the keyword table
